blocks.text: Model
blocks.source: Model

blocks.text: Modeling is an important aspect of synthetic biology, where scientists and researchers test and engineer the viable aspect of their final product prior to stepping foot into a laboratory. Our modelling workflow primarily deals with the reengineering of the BtSULT enzyme for 5β steroid specificity.
blocks.source:
Modeling is an important aspect of synthetic biology, where scientists and
researchers test and engineer the viable aspect of their final product prior to
stepping foot into a laboratory. Our modelling workflow primarily deals with the
reengineering of the BtSULT enzyme for 5 steroid specificity.

blocks.text: Enzyme Engineering
blocks.source: Enzyme Engineering

blocks.text: Wild type(WT) BtSULT is a sulfotransferase derived from Bacteroides thetaiotamicron that solubilizes steroid molecules such as DHEA. BtSULT was selected after its biochemical characterization by Yao et. al (2022), demonstrating sulfotransferase activity on bile acids. However, the substrate selectivity profile of BtSULT reveals its inability to accept 5β steroid molecules due to a flat A/B fusion ring, such as 5β-LCA. This fact necessitates an engineering process to redesign the WT BtSULT active site to sulfonate 5β-LCA for PCS treatment
blocks.source:
Wild type(WT) BtSULT is a sulfotransferase derived from Bacteroides
thetaiotamicron that solubilizes steroid molecules such as DHEA. BtSULT was
selected after its biochemical characterization by Yao et. al (2022), demonstrating
sulfotransferase activity on bile acids. However, the substrate selectivity profile of
BtSULT reveals its inability to accept 5 steroid molecules due to a flat A/B
fusion ring, such as 5 -LCA. This fact necessitates an engineering process to
redesign the WT BtSULT active site to sulfonate 5 -LCA for PCS treatment

blocks.text: BtSULT was selected as the main engineering scaffold instead of its mammalian homolog, SULT2A1, considering BL21 expression bottlenecks. SULT2A1 crystal structures were utilized from UniProt as a structural template for active-site redesign.
blocks.source:
BtSULT was selected as the main engineering scaffold instead of its mammalian
homolog, SULT2A1, considering BL21 expression bottlenecks. SULT2A1 crystal
structures were utilized from UniProt as a structural template for active-site
redesign.

blocks.text: The ideal reaction mechanism that indicates a working BtSULT mutant for wet-lab validation prioritizes sulfur-group transfer from PAPS to LCA 3-OH for production of sulfolithocholic acid, or sulfo-LCA.
blocks.source:
The ideal reaction mechanism that indicates a working BtSULT mutant for wet-lab
validation prioritizes sulfur-group transfer from PAPS to LCA 3-OH for production
of sulfolithocholic acid, or sulfo-LCA.

blocks.text: According to Kakuta et. al (1998), their study of human estrogen sulfotransferase activity asserts sulfuryl transfer is only possible if the catalytic base contacts the substrate OH at hydrogen bond range, 2.7 to 3.1 Å. This is to be considered in our engineering process.
blocks.source:
According to Kakuta et. al (1998), their study of human estrogen sulfotransferase
activity asserts sulfuryl transfer is only possible if the catalytic base contacts the
substrate OH at hydrogen bond range, 2.7 to 3.1 Å. This is to be considered in our
engineering process.

blocks.text: 1. Structural Study of BtSULT
blocks.source: 1. Structural Study of BtSULT

blocks.text: Although human SULT2A1 is well-studied and documented, BtSULT is not, requiring a study to identify candidates for a proposed catalytic base. Our early studies assumed BtSULT used histidine as a catalytic base, similar to His99 in human SULT2A1 (PDB: 1J99). Clustal Omega homology alignment tentatively suggested His215 as the closest histidine (Fig. 1). Extrapolating from the conserved PAPS binding motif, we also elect E136 as a catalytic base candidate. However, homology alignments were later disproved to be completely viable, partly due to the 15.2% sequence identity according to a Foldseek structural alignment (see below).
blocks.source:
Although human SULT2A1 is well-studied and documented, BtSULT is not,
requiring a study to identify candidates for a proposed catalytic base. Our early
studies assumed BtSULT used histidine as a catalytic base, similar to His99 in
human SULT2A1 (PDB: 1J99). Clustal Omega homology alignment tentatively
suggested His215 as the closest histidine (Fig. 1). Extrapolating from the
conserved PAPS binding motif, we also elect E136 as a catalytic base candidate.
However, homology alignments were later disproved to be completely viable,

blocks.text: However, Boltz-2 co-folding poses, where BtSULT was complexed with PAPS and LCA, suggested E144 as the closest deprotonating residue to LCA 3-OH. Although E144 contacted the substrate OH outside of H-bond distance, E144 was still selected to account for co-folding overcompensating for the stability of the output pose, something that is not completely representative of an enzyme’s tendency to change shape in its active site.

blocks.source: 2. Catalytic Distance Identification

blocks.text: In order to establish a baseline catalytic distance for which to discriminate between successfully and unsuccessfully engineered mutants, we are prompted to determine the optimal bond distance in SULT2A1-like enzymes.

blocks.text: The crystal structures of native SULT enzymes were analyzed for sulfuryl transfer and catalytic base distance, listed below. On average, sulfuryl transfer occurs at a distance of ~5 Å and catalytic bases are ~3 Å from the substrate OH (ref. Table 2).

blocks.text: Table 2: Catalytic Distance Inference from SULT Crystal Structures

Additionally, in order to identify residues blocking 5β-LCA binding, LCA was posed onto wild-type(WT) BtSULT using SULT2A1-DHEA(1J99) as a template. After superimposing BtSULT onto 1J99, the DHEA pose was transferred to dock LCA with emphasis on the anchored 3-OH position. Residue-substrate distances were measured to the LCA pose and a selectivity filter for steric clashes was applied to residues using MolProbity, with an overlap of >0.4 Å classified as a steric clash. The main pocket residues are displayed in Fig. 3

blocks.text: Although the greatest absolute clashes lie at Y158 and S150, studies of bile acid synthesis assert the importance of tyrosine in hydride transfer and brief analysis of the serine r-group dismissed it as an engineering focus due to a short, unpolar sidechain (Mindrich et al.). This shifted the focus to F147 as the principal steric clash, especially when considered as a selectivity market for 5β steroids in human carbonic anhydrases (Brynda et al.).

blocks.text: Round 0 of mutagenesis screening for the proposed enzyme prioritized a 6x-alanine scan, geared towards validating expression bottlenecks in-vitro prior to the final variant being reengineered. Steric clashes were changed to alanine as a proxy for catalytic activity in order to prioritize enzyme binding energy. This work was done prior to further structural studies, where Boltz-2 structural distances and review of literature confirmed the presence of mediating residues such as lysine, tyrosine, and glutamate as a divergent catalytic base to histidine in human AK1RD1. The mutations are as follows: E144A, W161A, K211A, F248A, F249A, T252A

blocks.text: 3.1 Point Mutation Panel
blocks.source: 3.1 Point Mutation Panel

blocks.text: The first technique draws from our structural studies by introducing point mutations into the active site of BtSULT. The proposed catalytic base of E144 was mutated to aspartate due to its similar yet shorter sidechain, with hopes to relieve a steric clash. Additionally, F147 was mutated to serine as a nonfunctional sidechain, testing if F147 was a selectivity marker for 5β steroids as it was in human carbonic anhydrases (Brynda et al.).
blocks.source:
The first technique draws from our structural studies by introducing point
mutations into the active site of BtSULT. The proposed catalytic base of E144 was
mutated to aspartate due to its similar yet shorter sidechain, with hopes to relieve a
steric clash. Additionally, F147 was mutated to serine as a nonfunctional sidechain,
testing if F147 was a selectivity marker for 5β steroids as it was in human carbonic
anhydrases (Brynda et al.).

blocks.text: In order to finalize F147’s mutation to serine, a saturation mutagenesis study was conducted, prioritizing transfer distance between the substrate and PAPS and base distance as a proxy for bond formation after mutating F147. The results are displayed in Table 3.
blocks.source:
In order to finalize F147’s mutation to serine, a saturation mutagenesis study was
conducted, prioritizing transfer distance between the substrate and PAPS and base
distance as a proxy for bond formation after mutating F147. The results are
displayed in Table 3.

blocks.text: Table 3: Saturation Mutagenesis of F147

Serine prioritized the lowest transfer distance and had the smallest base distance, suggesting the formation of an h-bond, now acting as a stabilizing residue to position the substrate more tightly into the catalytic pocket (Fig. 4).
blocks.source:
Serine prioritized the lowest transfer distance and had the smallest base distance,
suggesting the formation of an h-bond, now acting as a stabilizing residue to
position the substrate more tightly into the catalytic pocket (Fig. 4).

blocks.text: The first round of point mutations specifically searched for a switch between DHEA, the native substrate, and LCA selectivity in WT and mutated BtSULT. Such was done by mutating, in addition to mutations E144D and F147S, two PAPS motif residues R236 and T252 into R236K and T252S, probing the PAPS side geometry with a shorter reach and introducing a charge conserving residue, respectfully. His215 from then on was disproved as a catalytic base and mutations F147S seemed to decrease specificity for DHEA when the WT catalytic base was above the measured 2.91 Å OH distance in PDB 3F3Y.

blocks.text: The testing strategy was strengthened, introducing new sets of mutations in Boltz-2 poses only against complexes of LCA and PAPS, considering OH distance, sulfuryl transfer, and Y158 mediation of sulfuryl transfer. Additional candidates mutated E144 to histidine, utilizing SULT2A1’s catalytic histidine as a replacement to the proposed E144 catalytic base. T13’s earlier steric clash was relieved in further testing. These variants are shown in Table 4 and in Figure 4.

blocks.text: SULT2A1 loop 3 was split into its three functional segments for candidate design: its substrate binding region, the loop’s hinge region, and the PAPS binding motif. These three segments were interchanged across 10 variants along two segments of BtSULT plus additional flanking residues. Residues 153-190 hosted a BtSULT specific insertion, revealed by the initial ClustalOmega alignment and its proximity to the proposed E144 catalytic region. The substrate-binding region of SULT2A1 was grafted to this region. The C-terminus of BtSULT, aligning with SULT2A1’s catalytic loop, hosted either a grafted substrate-binding motif, a PAPS-binding motif, or both (Fig. 7).

blocks.text: Additionally, a 3X alanine background was added to each variant, following clash analysis of the 6X alanine background from Round 0 and Round 1. Glu144 and Lys211 had been assigned as key pocket residues and were therefore not mutated. Similarly, Trp161 was left unchanged due to its location in the 153-190 BtSULT insertion. This controlled our analysis of variants with grafts in the 153-190 region instead of adding a confounding variable (Fig. 8).

blocks.text: Although graft_Asp144 demonstrated the highest specificity for LCA in terms of maintaining catalytic distances for sulfuryl transfer, the substitution of the proposed catalytic base, Glu144, deemed this technique too experimental for a limited wet lab pipeline. Furthermore, F147S demonstrated the strongest specificity towards LCA. Although above the threshold for DCA catalysis, the F147S variant preserves Glu144. In addition to F147S, F147S_E144D was also chosen for in-vitro testing in order to validate the Glu→Asp hypothesis as an alternative catalytic base (Fig. 10).
